values.content:
=You are identifying the exact public job posting for a job originally found through a LinkedIn Job Alert.

ORIGINAL JOB:

Job title:
{{ $('filter Jobs').item.json.job_title }}

Company:
{{ $('filter Jobs').item.json.company }}

Location:
{{ $('filter Jobs').item.json.location }}

Original LinkedIn URL:
{{ $('filter Jobs').item.json.job_url }}

TAVILY SEARCH RESULTS:

{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}

YOUR TASK:

Review the provided search results and determine whether any result is the exact same vacancy or clearly the same job posting.

SOURCE PRIORITY:

1. Official company careers website
2. Official ATS platform such as Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, Comeet, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, or similar
3. Reputable external job board

MATCHING RULES:

- The company must match the original company.
- The job title must match exactly or be clearly equivalent.
- The location should be compatible with the original job.
- Do not choose another role simply because it contains similar keywords.
- Prefer the official company careers page or ATS whenever available.
- Do not invent URLs.
- source_url MUST be a URL that appears in the Tavily search results.
- Do not return the original LinkedIn URL as source_url.
- If the only matching result is LinkedIn, return posting_found = false.
- If there is meaningful uncertainty about whether the result is the same vacancy, return posting_found = false.
- It is better to return false than to attach the wrong job description.

SINGLE-POSTING RULE (very important):

- source_url must be the page of ONE specific job posting, where the full description of that one vacancy is shown.
- REJECT careers home pages (e.g. company.com/careers), "content" or "about" pages, company profile pages, job search result pages, location/category listing pages, and any page that lists many jobs.
- Good URLs usually contain a job ID or a job-specific path (e.g. /jobs/12345/..., /job/..., /job-details/..., greenhouse.io/.../jobs/123, myworkdayjobs.com/.../job/...).
- REJECT any linkedin.com URL, including country subdomains like il.linkedin.com.
- If the matching result's title shows a different seniority (e.g. "Senior ..." when the original is not senior), it is NOT the same vacancy.

If a confident match is found, return ONLY valid JSON:

{
  "company_name": "{{ $('filter Jobs').item.json.company }}",
  "posting_found": true,
  "source_url": "https://example.com/job",
  "source_type": "OFFICIAL_COMPANY",
  "match_confidence": "HIGH",
  "reason": "Brief explanation of why this result matches the original vacancy."
}

source_type must be exactly one of:

"OFFICIAL_COMPANY"
"ATS"
"JOB_BOARD"

match_confidence must be exactly one of:

"HIGH"
"MEDIUM"

If no result can be confidently matched, return ONLY:

{
  "posting_found": false,
  "source_url": "",
  "source_type": "",
  "match_confidence": "LOW",
  "reason": "No public search result could be confidently matched to the original vacancy."
}

Return only valid JSON.
Do not use Markdown.
Do not wrap the response in ```json.
Do not include text outside the JSON object.

=You are evaluating how suitable a job is for a Computer Science student who is looking primarily for junior, student, graduate, or entry-level roles in:

- Software Engineering
- Backend Development
- Full-Stack Development
- AI / GenAI
- AI Automation
- System Integration
- QA / Software Testing
- Other closely related technical positions


==================================================
CANDIDATE PROFILE
==================================================

[CANDIDATE PROFILE REDACTED FOR PUBLIC REPO - originally listed the candidate's programming languages, frameworks, AI/automation tools, and systems experience. Replace this block with your own skills and background before using.]

IMPORTANT:
Do NOT invent candidate experience, technologies, certifications, education, achievements, years of experience, or professional AI/ML experience that are not explicitly listed above.


==================================================
JOB INFORMATION
==================================================

Job title:
{{ $json.job_title }}

Company:
{{ $json.company }}

Location:
{{ $json.location }}

Original job URL:
{{ $json.job_url }}

Was a full public job description successfully found?
{{ $json.has_job_description }}

Public source URL:
{{ $json.source_url }}

Job posting content:
{{ $json.job_page_text }}


==================================================
YOUR TASK
==================================================

Evaluate how suitable this job is for the candidate.

Your evaluation should reflect whether the candidate could realistically apply for this position now.

Do not simply match keywords.

Consider:
- Seniority
- Required professional experience
- Mandatory technical skills
- Preferred / nice-to-have skills
- Education requirements
- Programming languages
- Frameworks
- Infrastructure / DevOps requirements
- AI / ML / LLM requirements
- QA / testing requirements
- System / integration requirements
- Management responsibilities
- Location and work-model restrictions when relevant


==================================================
IF A FULL JOB DESCRIPTION WAS FOUND
==================================================

If:

{{ $json.has_job_description }}

is true:

Base the evaluation primarily on the actual job description.

Identify the difference between:

1. Mandatory requirements
2. Preferred / nice-to-have requirements

Do NOT heavily penalize the candidate for missing a preferred requirement.

DO penalize strongly when the candidate is missing a clearly mandatory requirement.

Pay particular attention to required years of professional experience.

Examples:

- "1+ years experience" is a relatively small gap for a strong junior candidate
- "2+ years" should lower the score if clearly mandatory
- "3+ years" should significantly lower the score
- "5+ years" should heavily lower the score
- Senior / Lead / Principal / Manager roles should normally receive a low score unless the job description clearly indicates otherwise

Do not treat university projects or military technical experience as equivalent to several years of professional software-development experience unless the job itself allows equivalent experience.


==================================================
IF NO FULL JOB DESCRIPTION WAS FOUND
==================================================

If:

{{ $json.has_job_description }}

is false:

Evaluate using only:
- job title
- company
- location

Do NOT invent:
- required technologies
- required years of experience
- education requirements
- responsibilities
- seniority that is not apparent from the title

The confidence must be LOW.

Be conservative with the score.

A job should generally NOT receive a score above 75 when there is no job description unless the title itself clearly indicates a student, internship, graduate, junior, or entry-level position.


==================================================
SENIORITY CLASSIFICATION
==================================================

role_seniority must be exactly one of:

"STUDENT"
"INTERN"
"ENTRY_LEVEL"
"JUNIOR"
"MID"
"SENIOR"
"LEAD"
"PRINCIPAL"
"MANAGER"
"UNKNOWN"

Infer seniority from both the job title and the actual requirements.


==================================================
REQUIRED YEARS OF EXPERIENCE
==================================================

required_years_experience must be a short string, e.g. "0", "1+", "2+", "3-5", "UNKNOWN".

Use only what is actually stated or clearly supported by the job posting.


==================================================
SCORING GUIDELINES
==================================================

90-100: Excellent fit (student / junior / entry-level role, candidate matches nearly all requirements)
80-89: Strong fit, small gaps
70-79: Good / realistic fit
60-69: Possible fit, meaningful gaps
40-59: Weak fit
0-39: Poor fit (senior role, major experience gap, management-heavy, or clearly different field)


==================================================
RECOMMENDATION RULES
==================================================

If fit_score >= 70: recommendation = "APPLY"
If fit_score is between 55 and 69: recommendation = "MAYBE"
If fit_score < 55: recommendation = "DO_NOT_APPLY"


==================================================
OUTPUT FORMAT
==================================================

Return ONLY one valid JSON object:

{
  "job_title": "{{ $json.job_title }}",
  "company": "{{ $json.company }}",
  "location": "{{ $json.location }}",
  "job_url": "{{ $json.job_url }}",
  "fit_score": 0,
  "recommendation": "APPLY",
  "confidence": "HIGH",
  "role_seniority": "UNKNOWN",
  "required_years_experience": "UNKNOWN",
  "reason": "",
  "matching_skills": [],
  "missing_requirements": [],
  "mandatory_requirements_missing": [],
  "description_used": true
}

Do not output Markdown. Do not use ```json. Do not include commentary before or after the JSON. Do not invent information.

values.content:
=You are extracting job listings from a LinkedIn Job Alert email.

IMPORTANT:
- Read the ENTIRE email.
- Extract EVERY job listing in the email.
- Do not stop after the first job.
- Each separate company/job card is a separate job.
- Ignore introductory LinkedIn text such as "Your job alert has been created".
- Do not invent information.
- If there are 3 jobs, return 3 jobs. If there are 10 jobs, return 10 jobs.

For every job return:
- job_title
- company
- location
- job_url

Return ONLY valid JSON in exactly this format:

{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "job_title": "",
      "company": "",
      "location": "",
      "job_url": ""
    }
  ]
}

EMAIL START
{{ $json.text }}
EMAIL END
